title: policy-driven init liveness tuning and rollback safelist for private installs
author: Priya Nair
description:
Add a policy-driven init subsystem to the private installer Helm chart: introduce a typed values.schema entry 'initPolicies' that lets operators declare liveness/readiness tuning and a rollback safelist for resources that must be preserved across rollbacks. Motivation: recent on-prem upgrades revealed two production issues: 1) preflight init jobs would flake under tight probe defaults causing long upgrade churn; 2) some tenant-scoped resources (external secrets, cert-symlinks) were being removed during rollback because hooks relied on simple label matching. This PR provides a structured, backwards-compatible way to express probe overrides and an explicit rollback safelist that is consulted by the hook templates during break/failure flows.

What this changes (high level):
- values.schema.json: add 'initPolicies' block with typed fields (livenessProbe, readinessProbe, gracePeriodSeconds, rollbackSafelist). The schema includes examples and defaults.
- templates/_init_policy_helpers.tpl: new helper macros for generating probes and synthesizing safe names; used by init job templates and rollback hook.
- templates/init-job.yaml: consume initPolicies.* to set liveness/readiness probes and add jittered backoff via activeDeadlineSeconds when configured.
- templates/rollback-hook.yaml: consult .Values.initPolicies.rollbackSafelist to skip deletion of resources matching explicit kinds/names/labels; falls back to old behavior when unset.
- README-charts.md: document how to opt-in, examples for common on-prem scenarios, recommended probe defaults for slow NFS mounts.
- tests/chart-integration/: unit tests asserting templated probe fields and rollback safelist rendering.

Compatibility and migration notes:
- Default behavior unchanged: if initPolicies is omitted the templates preserve current defaults.
- Operators can migrate incrementally: set probe tuning first in non-critical tenants, then enable rollbackSafelist once validated.
- The rollback safelist supports 'kinds', 'names' and 'labelSelectors' so operators can be conservative.

Testing performed:
- Unit template tests with Helm template and kubeval schema checks.
- Local loop upgrade with helmfile on a dev VPC cluster (3-node on-prem mimic) exercising canary failure path.
- Integration test in CI renders chart with sample values and asserts that no deletion commands are rendered for safelisted items.

Rollout plan: merge to main, tag a patch chart release, ship as opt-in in the private-installer bundles. Monitor Canary upgrades and increase adoption via docs PR in private-installer repo.

Checklist:
- [x] values.schema updated and validated
- [x] templates use helpers (no repeated logic)
- [x] unit and integration tests added
- [x] docs/example included
- [x] reviewed and approved by SRE and Private Installer PM

Related: SUP-1298 (customer incident), ENG-8421 (initiative to harden upgrade rollback semantics)

review_comments: Evan Park: Can we avoid mutating names in helpers? If we change naming scheme later it may break downstream tooling. Suggest keeping original metadata.name where possible and use annotations for synthesized IDs.

Priya Nair (reply): Good point — updated helper to leave metadata.name intact and emit synthetic id into annotation 'redwood.internal/init-id'. Adjusted rollback hook to prefer names first, then annotation when present.
Sofia Martinez: Tests look good. One nit: the schema examples embed a 30s default that might be too small for slow NFS. Recommend 120s in examples and call out recommended values in docs.
Priya Nair (reply): Switched example defaults to 120s and added a note in README about tuning for NFS/Gluster workloads.
Liam Chen: What happens if someone sets rollbackSafelist to '*'? We should explicitly disallow wildcard-only safelists or warn heavily in docs.

Priya Nair (reply): Added validation guidance to README and an explicit schema note: wildcard '*' is allowed only as part of labelSelectors and will be flagged in upgrade notes. We intentionally avoid automated blocking, but added strong wording + a preflight lint job in CI to warn if '*' is used at top-level names/kinds.
Evan Park: CI flaked once on kubeval; re-run passed. Approving now.
release_notes: Introduce initPolicies for the private Helm chart: operators can tune liveness/readiness probes for init jobs and declare a rollback safelist to prevent deletion of critical tenant-scoped resources during rollbacks. Opt-in, backwards compatible. See README-charts.md for examples and migration guidance.
